deep.reconstruction:
The page has no text, only drawings, so this reading is interpretive.

(1) Main figure. A green circle bounds a disc. About 8 to 10 red (orange) pseudo-lines are drawn in it, i.e. simple curves crossing the boundary that pairwise intersect once inside. The disc is presumably the standard model of the projective plane: the disc with antipodal boundary points identified, the green circle being the line at infinity. Their ends on the circle are grouped in bundles, each labelled α0, α1, …, α7, with α8 = α0. This marks a cyclic enumeration of the ends (the 'directions at infinity'). The identity α8 = α0 indicates that going once round the line at infinity returns to the start, as the antipodal gluing requires. Several bundles meet at a single point on or just outside the circle (black dots at the top, bottom, left and right), so some lines are 'parallel', i.e. concurrent at infinity. Yellow hatching marks many cells of the arrangement. Most are triangular or lens-shaped, and many sit against the boundary. Blue and dark-green marks on the circle pick out boundary arcs between consecutive ends (the cells of the line at infinity, or the edges where boundary triangles meet it). The heavy dark-green arc between α3 and α4 on the left looks like an emphasised segment of the line at infinity. The likely aim is to list and locate the triangles, especially those touching the line at infinity, and to study how they are distributed (cf. Levi: every simple arrangement of n pseudo-lines has at least n triangles). It may equally concern the cell structure near infinity as one moves the line at infinity.

(2) Right figure. A vertical bundle of red pseudo-lines twists through a chain of pencilled circles. Inside each disc there are crossings; between discs there are blue or black bars where the bundle is pinched. One portion is scribbled out. This looks like cutting a long, braid-like (wiring-diagram-like) arrangement into local pieces, each a small sub-arrangement in its own disc, glued along short boundary segments. In other words, it resembles a composition or factorisation of arrangements, akin to writing a wiring diagram as a product of local configurations.

(3) Bottom figure. Two oriented lines a and b cross near a green horizontal line. Their arrows give the orientations, labelled a', b' on one side and a, b on the other. A dashed green curve bulges around the crossing, with faint pencil curves around it. This looks like a local study of a crossing passing through, or near, the line at infinity (or another reference line). It would be a deformation or flip move, recording how orientations and labels change (a→a', b→b'). It is related to Ringel's triangle-flip moves and to moving the line at infinity across a vertex.

(4) Bottom-left pencil. A fan of rays from a point, with a hatched angular sector and arcs of a circle. This suggests a pencil of lines through a point, i.e. lines concurrent at a vertex, and an angular sector of directions.

Overall this is exploratory combinatorial-topological work on 'systèmes de pseudo-droites'. It covers the cell structure of projective arrangements, triangles adjacent to the line at infinity, cyclic labelling of ends, and local decomposition and moves. It continues the disc, strip and fan diagrams of p.167.
errors: No checkable statements. The labelling of ends is somewhat irregular (several α2, α3, α4 labels appear twice, and α_x appears near α0/α8). This may reflect two different enumerations (two sides of the same end under the antipodal identification) rather than an error.

missed.claim: The right-hand chain-of-discs picture suggests an intended 'gluing/decomposition' calculus for pseudo-line systems, where a long arrangement is built from local pieces in discs joined along short boundary segments. This may anticipate operadic or categorical composition of arrangements. Nothing on the page develops it.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only as context for how Grothendieck approached pseudo-line combinatorics. The idea is closely related to the known wiring-diagram and higher-Bruhat machinery, so its novelty is doubtful.

deep.surprise_reason: The page holds purely exploratory drawings of pseudo-line arrangements, with triangle shading, cyclic labels at infinity and local moves. These are standard objects in the combinatorics of arrangements, and no statement or new result is visible.
transcription_corrections: The page contains no text beyond labels. Labels near the right end read 'α_x' and 'α_0' (written upside down) and should be treated as uncertain. The top-right label is 'α_8 = α_0' and is correct.

Faint mirror-image computer printout (an IBM job accounting listing: ACCOUNT NUMBER, JOBNAME, CPU TOTAL, RESOURCES ESTIMATED/USED) shows through from the reverse of the paper. It is not part of the notes.
The bottom figure's labels a', b' (top) and a, b (bottom) are correct and come with arrows indicating orientation.
